items.title: Rebuild Missing Files: add live progress (X of X) to the Extract action
items.why: Extracting a batch of missing files gives no feedback until the whole thing finishes -- director's own words: clicking a button with nothing happening always reads as 'is this broken?' The scan step already has this exact streaming-progress pattern; bring it to Extract too.
items.prompt:
Real live feedback: extracting a batch of missing files (Rebuild Missing Files, Step 2 report, 'Extract selected from archive') gives zero indication anything is happening until the whole batch finishes -- director's own words: 'when I click a button and nothing is happening I always wonder if an issue.' This can genuinely take a while for a big batch (just confirmed live extracting all of 'My GTS Audio Overhaul', dozens of mods/hundreds of files).

GROUNDING: this exact tool already has a working streaming-progress pattern one screen over -- the scan itself (`scanSession` in `web/rebuild-missing-routes.js`, `createSseSession` from `./sse-session`, `GET /api/rebuild-missing/scan/events`) streams `mod-scanned` events with `{index, total, collectionName, modName}`, and the client (`rmfHandleScanEvent` in `web/public/rebuild-missing-app.js`) renders them as `"{collectionName}: {index} / {total} — {modName}"` in `rmfScanLoadingText`. Mirror this SAME pattern for Extract -- don't invent a new progress mechanism.

SCOPE:
1. `POST /api/rebuild-missing/extract` (`web/rebuild-missing-routes.js` ~line 381): wrap the existing per-item `for (const item of items)` loop with the same SSE session pattern `scanSession` already uses -- a new `extractSession`, emitting a `mod-extracted` (or similar) event per item as it completes: `{index, total, name, ok}`. Same `GET /api/rebuild-missing/extract/events` shape as `/scan/events`.
2. Client (`web/public/rebuild-missing-app.js`, the `rmfExtractConfirmOkBtn` click handler ~line 461): instead of a bare `await rmfApi('POST', ...)` with nothing shown until it resolves, show a progress line the same way `rmfScanLoadingText` does -- something like a small inline status area near the Extract button, updating live as each `mod-extracted` event arrives: "{index} / {total} mods restored — {name}". Disable the Extract button and the confirm modal's own OK button while a batch is running, same as the scan already disables its own controls mid-run.
3. Keep the existing final summary callout (`rmfApplyExtractResults`'s success/warning text) as the completion state once the SSE stream reports done -- this is additive progress feedback during the run, not a replacement for the existing result summary.
4. Apply the SAME treatment to Download Archive if it's a multi-item batch action anywhere in this tool (check whether Download Archive is ever called for more than one row at a time) -- if it's always single-row, a plain busy-button state ("Downloading…", already present per the code read for this task) is enough there and doesn't need full SSE progress.

VERIFY live against a real, largish batch (e.g. 'My GTS Audio Overhaul', the same collection just used to confirm the underlying extraction now works after the 413 fix) -- confirm the progress line updates per mod in real time, confirm the final summary still shows correctly once done, and confirm a small/fast batch (1-2 files) doesn't feel janky with the added progress UI (a near-instant complete should still render cleanly, not flash unreadably). Handoff with what you tested.

items.title: New Reports tab: Workshop Report (per-collection Nexus timestamps + staging folder link)
items.why: Director needed a real way to tell which Workshop collections they've actually edited recently -- Nexus's own collection page shows a frozen creation-time date for private collections. Found the real signal live this session (the per-REVISION updatedAt, not the collection-level one) and it checked out against the director's own memory of editing "My Dragonborn UI for GTS" on 8/13.
items.prompt:
New report, mockup approved: `design/vortex-workshop-report-mockup.html` (Approved 2026-08-14). A new "Workshop Report" sub-tab under Reports (`web/public/index.html`'s `area-reports` section, alongside the existing 4 sub-tabs -- Stats/Work Through/Update Compare/Rules Generator -- follow their exact `reports-sub-*` button + `reports-sub-area-*` div pattern).

REAL FINDING BEHIND THIS (grounding, don't re-derive): live-tested against the director's own Nexus data this session. Nexus's `Collection.updatedAt` (the collection record itself) is frozen at creation and never moves. But `CollectionRevision.updatedAt` (per-revision -- already fetched by this codebase's existing `fetchCollectionRevisions` in `lib/nexus-collection-download.js`, used for the revision picker) DOES move when a private/unlisted collection's content is edited -- confirmed against "My Dragonborn UI for GTS": revision `updatedAt` was 2026-08-13T23:23:54Z, and the director independently confirmed that's genuinely when they last edited it. THIS is the timestamp the report shows -- not `Collection.updatedAt`.

DATA SOURCES (reuse, don't reimplement):
1. Collection list + slugs: reuse the same Vortex-DB read `ff37c49` already added (`collection-runner.js`'s `loadSyncStateBatch`, surfaces both collections WITH a local `collection.json` and ones without, each with `collectionSlug`) -- same `isVortexRunning()` gate as that route.
2. Per-collection revision info: reuse `fetchCollectionRevisions(apiKey, slug)` from `lib/nexus-collection-download.js` (already returns `revisions: [{revisionNumber, revisionStatus, createdAt, updatedAt}]`, sorted newest-first) -- take `revisions[0]` for revision number, status (draft/published pill), and the `updatedAt` to display. No new Nexus query logic needed, this function already exists and is already used elsewhere in this app.
3. Staging folder path: the same `stagingModDir`/folder-name resolution `listPickableCollections` already has for collections that DO have a local `collection.json`; collections without one show "Not downloaded yet" in that cell instead (no folder to open).
4. Open Staging Folder action: reuse the existing `open-staging-folder` route/handler (see Rebuild Missing Files' own `rmfOpenStagingFolder` / `POST /api/rebuild-missing/open-staging-folder`) rather than writing a new one.
5. View on Nexus link: reuse the existing `nexusCollectionUrl(slug, revisionNumber)` helper already used elsewhere (`web/public/app.js`).

PROGRESS / PACING -- flagged during design review, worth addressing deliberately: a live Nexus call PER collection could be slow and risks hitting Nexus's rate limits for a director with many Workshop collections (17+ seen live this session). Run these sequentially, not a parallel blast, and stream progress the SAME way the just-added scan/extract progress patterns already do (`createSseSession`, an SSE endpoint, `{index, total, name}` events) -- the mockup's own progress line (`"Checking '{name}' — {index} / {total}"` + a progress bar) expects this. Cache the result (`Last checked: X ago`, per the mockup) rather than re-querying Nexus every time the report tab is opened -- only refetch on an explicit **Check Nexus for updates** click, matching this app's own "manual action, not automatic live-state read" convention used everywhere else Nexus/Vortex-state gets touched.

TABLE COLUMNS (per mockup): Collection name, Slug/ID (monospace), Revision number + a draft/published pill (reuse the pill visual language already established for status badges elsewhere in this app), Last updated on Nexus (absolute date/time + a relative "X ago" line under it), Actions (Open Staging Folder or "Not downloaded yet", plus View on Nexus).

VERIFY live: run the real check against the director's actual Workshop collections, confirm the progress line updates per collection, confirm "My Dragonborn UI for GTS" shows a revision `updatedAt` the director can independently recognize as correct (same number already confirmed this session: 2026-08-13T23:23:54Z), confirm Open Staging Folder actually opens the right folder, confirm a collection with no local `collection.json` shows "Not downloaded yet" instead of a broken folder action. Handoff with what you tested.
